summary: Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya was an Indologist and philosopher. He taught Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan and held positions at Vidyasagar College (professor attested 1970–1975, attested 1990) and the University of Calcutta's Department of Sanskrit (lecturer attested 1982, attested 1994).

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen in 1999 and held posts at Leipzig University (attested 2005) and Heidelberg University (attested 2007–2009).

Muhammad Ashraf Khan works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as Deputy Director at Taxila Museum, Director of the Department of Archaeology and Museums in Andhra Pradesh, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019).

Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Hanazono University (~1920–1925) and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as abbot of Shofukuji (~1949–1978), president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), and head of the Institute for Zen Studies (1964).

Mun-keat Choong is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute, Komazawa University (BA ~1986–1990), and the University of Queensland, earning an MA (~1991–1994) supervised by Roderick S. Bucknell and a PhD (~1994–1998).

Munenobu Sakurai (b. 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1986–1991), became an assistant professor at Iwate University (~1995–2004), and was appointed professor at Tohoku University (~2004).

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Kyoto University (~1969–1971) and Harvard University (PhD ~1971–1975). He was assistant professor at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1978–1989), then assistant professor (~1989–1990) and professor (~1990–2008) at Kyoto University.

Muneyoshi Yanagi (1889–1961) was a philosopher and scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki and completed his studies at the University of Tokyo (~1910–1913).

Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar in religious studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied under Brigitte Marschall and earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (attested 2010).

Murray Barnson Emeneau (1904–2005) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale (PhD under Franklin Edgerton). He taught Latin at Yale (1926) and served as professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at UC Berkeley (1940–1971).

Musashi Tachikawa (b. 1942) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at Nagoya University and Harvard (PhD under Daniel H. H. Ingalls), he held posts at Nagoya University, National Museum of Ethnology, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Muzaffar Alam (b. 1947) is a scholar of history, Indology, and Central Asian studies. Educated at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and JNU (PhD), he taught at JNU (~1979–2001) before becoming a professor at the University of Chicago (~2001).

Myles Dillon (1900–1972) was a linguist and Indologist educated at University College Dublin. He taught Sanskrit and philology at Trinity College Dublin (1928–1930) and UCD (1930–1937), and later served as director of the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (1960–1968).
Myokyo-ni (1921–2007) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Graz and undertook traditional training under Sōkō Morinaga between roughly 1960 and 1976.
Myoshin Fujitake is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and was a committee member of the Otani Academic Society (attested 2000).

Mysore Hiriyanna (1871–1950) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned degrees at Madras Christian College. He served as a librarian, teacher, and later Professor of Sanskrit Studies at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and the University of Mysore (~1912–1927).

Myōsei Tatsuguchi (b. 1934) is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Diane E. Riggs and Jeff Wilson. He served as a professor (attested 1987) and professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Ryukoku University.

Mónika Kiss is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She studied as a doctoral student in Japanese studies at Eötvös Loránd University under advisors and teachers Masanori Yamaji, Robert F. Rhodes, and Nozomu Saito.

N. A. Jayawickrama (b. 1920) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Peradeniya (~1958–1969) and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1979–1985).
N. Aiyaswami Sastri was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).
